newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar closes higher in volatile trading.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar closes higher in volatile trading.

text.p: "I really believe the underlying trend is upward and I know that on balance it has tended to be a bit weak recently after the American interest rate move," Thiessen told reporters.

The U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points on March 25 to halt signs of rising inflation in the U.S. economy. That move triggered a shift by investors to hold U.S. securities at the expense of Canadian-dollar denominated assets.
Before today's rally, the Canadian dollar had fallen five percent since January.

"The idea that the bank is going to switch to a less stimulative monetary policy comes as a relief to the foreign exchange market," said Rob Palombi, senior fixed-income analyst for MMS International.
"This rally is all about what is going right for the Canadian economy," Palombi said.
Analysts also said U.S. data indicating that consumer prices had remained largely unchanged was also favorable for the Canadian dollar.
The U.S. Labor Department reported that the monthly Consumer Price Index (CPI) increased 0.1 percent in April.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar fell to 84.36 yen from Wednesday's close of 84.40 and dipped to 1.2360 marks from Wednesday's 1.2367 marks.
